Compute it on the fly - before computing the scaled loss - will only work in a single replica and in a single gradient accumulation setting. Because we want to update the model's parameters by using a `global batch`, but when we enter `training_step`, it is already in a single replica context, and the batch received is just a partial batch, therefore we can't access the global batch distributed anymore.

There is a potential subtlety here. Since we use 

    self.args.strategy.experimental_distribute_dataset(ds),

depending on the `strategy` and the hardware (single/multi CPU/GPU/TPU) settings, the `batch` in `self.distributed_training_steps` could be usual tensors, or could be packed in `PerReplica` object, something like

	PerReplica:{
	  0: <tf.Tensor: shape=(2,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([57, 94], dtype=int32)>,
	  1: <tf.Tensor: shape=(2,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([22, 70], dtype=int32)>,
	  2: <tf.Tensor: shape=(2,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([10, 77], dtype=int32)>,
	  3: <tf.Tensor: shape=(2,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([64, 82], dtype=int32)>,
	  4: <tf.Tensor: shape=(1,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([22], dtype=int32)>,
	  5: <tf.Tensor: shape=(0,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([], dtype=int32)>,
	  6: <tf.Tensor: shape=(0,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([], dtype=int32)>,
	  7: <tf.Tensor: shape=(0,), dtype=int32, numpy=array([], dtype=int32)>
	}

This is what I had (for a personal project) when I used TPU v3-8. However, I don't know if there are other types of distributed objects when we use different strategy. If possible, could you try what types a distributed batch would be in a multiple GPU environment? 

@jplu , do you think it is good to assume it is either a tuple of 2 tensors, or a tuple of 2 perplica objects? In both cases, a tuple will be a (features, labels) pair.

remark: [PerReplica](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/v2.3.0/tensorflow/python/distribute/values.py#L365)

```
    @tf.function

is included in that graph, the graph will have the initial value of `self.nb_instances_in_global_batch` the first time it is compiled. Even we recompute it outside the graph, the value is still the initial value in the graph.

No, our internal discussions which resulted in the current [README](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers#why-should-i-use-transformers) (see point 4) are that we should copy and paste code so that our models are self-contained and easy to tweak to the cost of redundancy. The only inheritance we accept is for things like `Flaubert` or `XLM-RoBERTa` when the models are exactly the same as another model of the library (and we just have new classes for the proper names).

@qiweizhen @JetRunner - I think this is not fully correct here... 
IMO, it should be `if past_key_values is not None:` and not `if use_cache:`.

The problem is that by default `use_cache=True` (during inference). If someone then passes some `decoder_input_ids` with seq_length > 1, no `causal_mask` will be calculated and the result is wrong. During training `use_cache=False` anyways so there was no problem, but this should be fixed for inference IMO. 

I think we should change it to:

```python
if past_key_values not None:
       assert hidden_states.size(0) == 1, "At the moment `use_cache` is only supported for `decoder_input_ids` of length 1"
...
```

instead of

if use_cache:
...

This PR is wonderful! `parametrized.expand` is a great find, and not saving static embeddings is an obvious win. We should add the latter to bart in a separate PR.

The expansion of embeddings may require a bit more care, but the comment below doesn't prevent merging this PR. You can just delete that logic later if it is bad.


### Expanding Positional Embeddings
```python
if max_pos > self.weight.size(0): # recompute/expand embeddings if needed
```

The reason I haven't autoexpanded the bart positional embeddings so far is that I wanted an error for long sequences that the model would translate poorly, instead of just poor performance. But if you can like concatenate a few en-ru examples and see that performance doesn't plummet it would be good. There is also a theoretical O(seq_len^2) theoretical cost associated with passing longer documents through transformers, so we may not want to encourage longer docs/instead write tooling that, for example, uses moses `SentenceSplitter` to chunk documents, pass them through the model, and rejoin the results correctly. If it just works with the auto expansion hack then I'm all for it.

body:
_out-of-scope:_
I'm not a big fan of overriding a method when subclassing either to be honest. *E.g.* I think it's good practice to have a 
```python 
def parent_class_method(...):
      raise NotImplementedError()
```
so that the sub-classes are forced to implement the method (assuming that the sub-classes have at least two sub-classes which implement this function differently). 
**but** I think it's bad practice to have a 
```python
def parent_class_method(...):
     ### logic that applies for 90% of subclasses
    ...
```
and then overwrite this method only for the subclasses which require a different behavior. I think this case should be avoided because it is not very readable and can lead to problems if people don't see that the method was overwritten.
I would for example force in `generation_utils` to have `prepare_logits_for_generation()` to have a `NotImplementedError()` abstract method, which we currently don't have...

Just as a side-not to communicate my inheritance opinions in general:D What do you think?

=> Now taking this to the extreme, I would have not overwritten the `missing_keys` attribute either. But in the case of this PR, I am 100% fine with keeping the old logic for consistency and because it is really not hard / important to understand where this class attribute is set for the user. So will revert this change to how it was before.
author: patrickvonplaten

body:
I wouldn't say it's bad practice since it's what every OO course teaches you to do ;-) I guess it depends on the goal and the readability you aim to. I would say your approach is better for things we want to expose to users and think modifications/customization are going to be often done (a bit like our approach to the modeling files) but for internal things, it's okay to use the traditional OO approach.

Anyhow, do what you want for those class attributes are you are the ones actually writing this PR, it was just my two cents ;-)

body:
```suggestion
*Building open-domain chatbots is a challenging area for machine learning research. While prior work has shown that scaling neural models in the number of parameters and the size of the data they are trained on gives improved results, we show that other ingredients are important for a high-performing chatbot. Good conversation requires a number of skills that an expert conversationalist blends in a seamless way: providing engaging talking points and listening to their partners, and displaying knowledge, empathy and personality appropriately, while maintaining a consistent persona. We show that large scale models can learn these skills when given appropriate training data and choice of generation strategy. We build variants of these recipes with 90M, 2.7B and 9.4B parameter models, and make our models and code publicly available. Human evaluations show our best models are superior to existing approaches in multi-turn dialogue in terms of engagingness and humanness measurements. We then discuss the limitations of this work by analyzing failure cases of our models.*
```

Thanks for the PR!

Just one comment, you just have to modify the `TFTrainer` not the `TFPretrainedModel` because a saved model has to be created only after a training. 

Basically the method `TFTrainer.save_model(self, output_dir)` must become:

```
def save_model(self, output_dir):
    output_dir = output_dir if output_dir is not None else self.args.output_dir
    logger.info("Saving model in {}".format(output_dir))
    if isinstance(self.model, TFPreTrainedModel):
        self.model.save_pretrained(output_dir)
    else:
        self.model.save_weights(output_dir)
    tf.saved_model.save(self.model, output_dir)
```

And `TFPreTrainedModel.save_pretrained(self, save_directory)` must stay as it is.

body:
This is a great PR!! Lots of welcome improvements and will be easier to develop TF models!

Not reviewing any doc/individual code as its a draft PR, just the behavior.

I have a few questions: 

### From embedding building to `tf.keras.layers.Embedding`

The word embeddings currently rely on `tf.name_scope('word_embeddings): [...] self.add_weight [...]`, and you updated that to use `tf.keras.layers.Embedding`. That's cool, but now you're not passing these weights around to models with LM heads to be used by the decoders, while the input and output embeddings should be tied in most `ForMaskedLM` and `WithLMHead` models. 

- Would we now be relying on the LM head weights being in the checkpoint?

### Dense -> DenseEinsum

- Does the change from `tf.keras.layers.Dense` to `tf.keras.layers.experimental.EinsumDense` imply a breaking change or some magic that we must do to ensure that the weights get correctly loaded? 
- Is that change the main one that unlocks better performance?

### Tuples -> tf.TensorArray

You're stacking the tensor array in the model outputs, but that returns stacked tensors instead of the previous tuples, which is a big breaking change.

- Why is that change necessary? Does it give better performance? Is it necessary for graph mode?

### Joining the `nsp` + `mlm` in one `cls`

- This is cool as it's more similar to what we do in PyTorch! However, you're now handling the names of the weights directly in the `modeling_tf_utils.py` file. I cannot imagine that scales as more models are converted to this implementation?
author: LysandreJik

First, the changes in this PR are awesome! The speed-up we can gain from these changes is more than important and having a more "fine-grained" load_weights function in TF is essential to be able to add models like `TFEncoderDecoderModel`. So that's huge!

One suggestion from my side would be to maybe concentrate this PR only on these two things and only on BERT. So all I would do in this PR would be:

- Add all those amazing "non-breaking" speed-ups for BERT & 
- Add the new `load_weights` function that if I understood correctly can be added without breaking **any** backwards compatibility and without having to introduce the string replacements.

After this is finished IMO, it would be great to merge the PR and after that we could:

- add the optimizations for other models
- flip the `return_dict=True` switch (I don't think this should be  done here - as it affects all PT models as well)
- discuss whether we want to do the parameter renaming

The advantage would be:
a) Easier to review
b) Less potential merge conflicts
c) Safer in a sense that we can play around with the new weight loading functions and see how it works without changing weight parameter names.

Thanks for all your hard work and optimization for the TFBert model, that's very cool!

One general note: fixing completely unrelated bugs in the same PR is not good practice as:

1. it slows down the fix for every other user since this a big PR that needs a lot of love

On the comments related to this PR specifically now, the big problem is that we cannot change the global switch of `return_dict` now. Depending on the time needed to finish the TF push, there might be intermediate releases before v4 where we can't afford to have that breaking change. There is a crude way to have that switch set to True for the TFBert models just now I suggested in the comments and there is probably some clever way with a private flag that could allow us to add the TF models one by one with a new default without breaking anything. All tests are passing is not an excuse for an instant breaking change on the whole library. There may be releases between now and the v4. This change can only be made once we go to v4. In the meantime, the switch can be activated:
- by ignoring the config value in TFBertMainLayer and just storing `True`. This removes the possibility of setting it to False via the config momentarily, but it can still be passed in the forward in eager mode.
- in all TF models by adding this line in the init of `TFPreTrainedModel`.

To first merge this PR without too many changes, I would favor using the first solution for now, then switch to all TF models later on when they are updated, and only do the global switch on the eve of the v4 release.

body:
don't merge yet, I don't think it should live here after sleeping on it. I think this should make its way upstream! Barrier is just waiting for all distributed processes (if any) to sync (like a join).  I think what's happening is we get to `os.listdir` on rank 1 before rank 0 has saved the checkpoint. 

rank 0 deletes the old checkpoint, and saves a new checkpoint which needs to happen before this os.listdir call!

I think the solution should be that DDP waits for this process to completes, before returning.

`evaluate` and `predict` make use of `get_eval_dataloader` and `get_test_dataloader`, which in turn both call `_get_eval_sampler`.

```python

you would expect to get the most commonly used / standard BERT config being `bert-base-cased`, which is useful information IMO. The only other option that would make sense is to force the user to configure everything by himself, but I think putting random parameters there makes no sense. 

And since it's a big question of consistency with the library (we will not go back from having default configs I think), I see only the "real" default parameters option as the way to go.

author: patrickvonplaten

body:
I think @patrickvonplaten has the right intentions  following what is established across the repo. In every configuration file (e.g., [BERT](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/src/transformers/configuration_bert.py#L55), [ALBERT](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/src/transformers/configuration_albert.py#L37), [CTRL](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/src/transformers/configuration_ctrl.py#L30-L31)), we have defaults for configurations so that initializing one without arguments yields a sensible architecture based on existing pre-trained weights. If it is not the case for a model, then it slipped the review and should be updated.

This means that doing: `BertModel(BertConfig())` yields a model similar to what the original BERT model is. This makes it easier to work with as we don't have a myriad of (usually different) arguments to supply to each configuration when doing tests.

Also, this is the convention we have adopted until now and I see no strong argument against it that would lead to changing this convention. I also see no argument on why FSMT would need to differ in that regard.

@stas00:
> Because the configuration process for fsmt was complex, using some defaults originally masked problems, so by not having defaults it was detecting problems of not getting the right config immediately. I'm concerned that adding defaults that look about right all kinds of unexpected problems may arise.

I would say that if some problems were masked by using some defaults, then some additional tests should be added to ensure that these tests are not an issue, either for this model or for others.

body:
Why not just add `truncation="longest_first"` at the tokenizer call?

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/098ddc2244ece7fe1942e38237c08c2b576291d5/src/transformers/pipelines.py#L673-L686

This works for RoBERTa as the tokenizer has `max_len` set to 512, not 514, which is not the case for `max_position_embeddings`.

I guess we could have put `config.max_position_embeddings=512` and then just initialize the embeddings using `config.max_position_embeddings + 2`, but it would be a big breaking change now (requires to update all the RoBERTa configurations).

We didn't do it like this at first as the `RobertaEmbeddings` inherited from `BertEmbeddings`:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/d8b641c8393f1f7ce0ec0d0a1f7c1cefcd966971/transformers/modeling_roberta.py#L39-L56

import logging

Hi! Thanks a lot @NielsRogge for implementing this model! It's a great model that definitely deserves its place in the huggingface library, and you did a great job implementing it! I'm reviewing the code below.

Regarding the tokenizer, we do not have a dependency (hard or soft) on pandas, but we will soon have one on `datasets`. I think it is feasible to have `datasets` as the central object for tabular data instead of pandas dataframes. It's very easy to use it as a replacement, your example code would simply use a `datasets.Dataset` instead of a `pd.Dataframe`:
```py
from transformers import TapasTokenizer
from datasets import Dataset

data = {'Actors': ["Brad Pitt", "Leonardo Di Caprio", "George Clooney"], 
        'Age': ["56", "45", "59"],
        'Number of movies': ["87", "53", "69"],
        'Date of birth': ["18 december 1963", "11 november 1974", "6 may 1961"]}

table = Dataset.from_dict(data)
queries = ["When was Brad Pitt born?", 
           "Which actor appeared in the least number of movies?",
           "What is the average number of movies?"]

tokenizer = TapasTokenizer.from_pretrained("tapas-base-finetuned-wtq")
inputs = tokenizer(table=table, queries=queries)
```
Putting @lhoestq in cc.

Regarding the configuration and tokenizer, it would be great to uncouple them from their BERT counterparts. 

I haven't played around with the model yet, but it seems to be in a great shape already. If you can do the modifications in the review here that would be great, and then I'll spend time playing with it and will come back to you regarding the tokenizer API currently setup.

Concerning git, it seems you have *just* rebased & force-pushed, so that's very cool. Regarding your question, this does mess up the history of users that are currently using your branch, but seeing as we're early in development, there shouldn't be any.

body:
I've played around with your implementation, and it works well! It's very cool. Now comes a complicated aspect: ensuring we stay consistent with the existing API, especially for the tokenizers.

This is a complicated part, so please let us know if you would like some help along the way/if you want us to take over from here, in which case we would open PRs against your branch with proposals.

Some of this echoes what you've put in your PR description, I'm putting it here as well so that we don't lose track of what's left to do.

### Tokenizers

As you've said, the tokenizer might be a bit hard to use with our existing API, but I think it's possible. Let's list the issues with the current implementation:

Right now, the tokenizer is not behaving as we would like as it doesn't respect much of the flags passed to it. For example, running your example:

```py
from transformers import TapasTokenizer

dir_name = "./tapas_base_finetuned_wtq_with_reset_and_intermediate_pretraining"

tokenizer = TapasTokenizer(vocab_file=dir_name + "/vocab.txt", model_max_length=512)
encoded_inputs = tokenizer.batch_encode_plus(table=table, queries=queries)
```
This immediately pads to the maximum length. This is the case whether I specify the `padding` strategy or not. It does not respect the `truncation` parameter either, nor does it respect the `return_attention_mask`, but it does respect the `return_token_type_ids`.

I haven't tried the `pad_to_multiple_of`, `is_split_into_words`, `return_overflowing_tokens`, `return_special_tokens_mask`, `return_length` parameters, but having them work similarly to other tokenizers should be a priority.

#### `__call__`

The `__call__` method should be implemented for the tokenizer. The following methods should also be implemented:

:warning: some of these are already implemented in the superclass, and may not need to be reimplemented. This may be the case for `prepare_for_model`, which takes care of the truncation/padding on its own.

- `build_inputs_with_special_tokens`
- `get_special_tokens_mask`
- `create_token_type_ids_from_sequences`

It seems you've only implemented the batching methods, but there are methods to be used for single sequences as well:

- `encode_plus`
- `prepare_for_model`

### Testing 

#### Modeling Tapas Utilities

Same as the other utilities, it would be nice to have this in the main file. Moving `test_modeling_tapas_utilities.py` to be in the same file as `test_modeling_tapas.py` would be great.

#### Tokenization tests

The implementation of the tokenization tests would be a good way to monitor what is currently working/failing.

body:
The reason these are called `label_ids` is that one of the 7 token type ids which the authors of TAPAS define is called `prev_label_ids`. These indicate which tokens were part of an answer to the previous table-question pair, which is useful in a conversational set-up. Using `_ids` at the end reflects that these are similar to `input_ids` (also having shape `(batch_size, sequence_length)`, but are zero or one depending on whether a token is (part of) an answer. So IMO it's more clear to use `label_ids` rather than `labels`, otherwise people might be confused when they see `prev_label_ids` in the docs. 

Labels which are really similar to other `labels` in the Transformers library are the `aggregation_labels` to train `TapasForQuestionAnswering` and `labels` to train `TapasForSequenceClassification`.

1) If `decoder_embeddings.weight.size() != encoder_embeddings.weight.size()`, then let's set `self.config.tie_encoder_decoder_word_embeds = False` so that it is saved as `False` automatically afterwards. Setting `config.tie_encoder_decoder_word_embeds` to `False`..."`

2) I think we should also add a `logger.info(...)` if "`type(encoder.config.__class__) != type(decoder.config.__class__)` saying that  encoder and decoder are different classes and that the user should make sure that tying the word embedding matrices is the desired behavior and if not he should disable it with `model.config.tie_encoder_decoder_word_embeds = False`. body:
I agree that it is too bold to tie embedding matrices by default that are different in value.

If embedding matrices are the same, in 99% of the cases the models are the same.
Now it is hard for me to imagine when the user may want to tie embeddings but not entire models (according to paper tying entire models is the best strategy). 

I actually made a false assumption that tying embeddings between models like longformer and roberta is always a good idea. Following the principle of least surprise and the philosophy of ''huggingface' library, it actually seems better to leave the option `model.encoder.word_embeddings = model.decoder.word_embeddings` to the user and not take out separately the embeddings tying from entire models tying.

body:
Cool, thanks for the work on this! Leveraging the `fit` function is probably a better idea than trying to reinvent the wheel ourselves. I like the general design, but I have a few comments/questions.

## 1. Input data

The PyTorch side of the library (and all the PyTorch scripts) have datasets that eventually yield dictionaries containing all inputs of the model as well as the labels. In an ideal world, it would be great if we could leverage that format easily for TF as well (so that the same script can be used for PT and TF by just changing a few lines, especially when using the datasets library). I don't know if that's possible or not but one thing to explore more I believe.

## 2. Optimizer and scheduler

I like the new optimizer for gradient accumulation a lot. This feels like a very good design. Should we deprecate `GradientAccumulator`?
But where are the schedulers? Is this something you intend to control via callbacks? If that's the case I didn't see one with a sensible default (the linear + warmup used in PT for instance).

## 3. Callbacks

Leveraging Keras callbacks is definitely a good idea. My only remark here is that is should be more customizable. On the PT side we have some default callbacks and the init takes a list of additional callbacks the user can add.

## 4. Metrics

I'm not in favor of adding a new file of metrics we will have to maintain forever. We should provide an adapter for datasets `Metric` object and rely on the datasets library (or existing Keras metrics if users prefer them) but they shouldn't be in the transformers library (on the PT we will soon deprecate the ones in the metric folder).
author: sgugger

Data is going to be a bit more complicated than a tuple in general. The PyTorch API (and the datasets library) uses dictionaries as input. If we could be closer to PyTorch and support dict in general (with and y would be the value under the key "labels" in that case) that would be easier (in terms of switching a script from PyTorch to TF).

Also how would that function work when the model expects multiple labels (pretraining objectives or question-answering problems)?

body:
data is always a tuple of size 3 maximum `(train_data, labels, sample_weights)` and `sample_weights` is added only if the parameter is filled in the `.fit()` method otherwise data is of size 2.

In our case, `train_data` are a dictionary and `labels` is either a Tensor or a dictionary. Dictionary in the case of question answering task for example.

For tasks such as question answering the `.compile()` method has to be called a bit differently because we have two outputs `start` and `end` logits. So the call becomes:

```
self.model.compile(optimizer=self.optimizer, loss={'output_1': self.model.compute_loss, 'output_2': self.model.compute_loss, metrics={"output_1": self.metrics, "output_2": self.metrics})
```

`output_1` and `output_2` are the name of the two outputs by default. But this will change to their real names `start_logits` and `end_logits`, I just need to do several changes for that.

However, there are many factors that determine the encoding for specific things (`locale`, sys encoding, environment variables but even OS and Python versions!). As an example: the default decoding differs for me when using my editors built-in terminal and PowerShell and CMD. On top of that `locale.getpreferredencoding` differs from `sys.stdin.encoding`, and they differ between Python versions.

I do not have the time to look into this further to figure out what the best, cross-platform, cross-Python-version way is to deal with this. As for now, since the output of `git --version` is simple enough without special chars, I think we can stick with UTF-8.

For those interested, [this is a nice PEP](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0597/) that talks about the slow move to defaulting utf-8 in Python across the board.

        def softmax(_outputs):

            return shifted_exp / shifted_exp.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
```

body:
It is not true that the other application doesn't need encoder outputs. When calling the teacher decoder, if student and teacher encoders are different, the right thing to do is to pass the teacher encoder outputs, and as we can see from these lines, even in the original case, we could have `self.different_encoder` be true if not all layers were copied from teacher to student: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/02bdfc025169a301a57f48a7642c69de3d10a2db/examples/seq2seq/distillation.py#L60-L61.
So I think we do need to extract teacher encoder outputs inside this `if different_encoder` block.
However, we can extract hidden states optionally based on whether we need to calculate hidden loss or not. I have the following modified code which passes the unit tests. Please lmk what you think.
```
        if self.different_encoder:  # compute encoder hidden state loss
            with torch.no_grad():
                teacher_encoder = self.teacher.get_encoder()(
                    input_ids,
                    attention_mask=src_mask,
                    output_hidden_states=self.do_calc_hidden_loss,
                    return_dict=True
                )
            teacher_enc_outputs = teacher_encoder.last_hidden_state
            if self.do_calc_hidden_loss:
                teacher_enc_hid = teacher_encoder.hidden_states
                hid_loss_enc = self.calc_hidden_loss(
                    src_mask,
                    enc_hidden_state,

Ok I have another fix that's passing unit tests. Please lmk what you think. I renamed the `self.do_calc_hidden_loss` to `self.different_base_models` because really that's what it was keeping track of, and the boolean value is flipped from the earlier one. 

```
        if self.different_encoder:  # compute encoder hidden state loss
            with torch.no_grad():
                teacher_encoder = self.teacher.get_encoder()(
                    input_ids,
                    attention_mask=src_mask,
                    output_hidden_states=not self.different_base_models,
                    return_dict=True
                )
            if self.different_base_models:
                teacher_enc_outputs = teacher_encoder.last_hidden_state
            else:
                teacher_enc_hid = teacher_encoder.hidden_states
                hid_loss_enc = self.calc_hidden_loss(
                    src_mask,
                    enc_hidden_state,
                    teacher_enc_hid,
                    self.e_matches,
                    normalize_hidden=self.hparams.normalize_hidden,
                )

        teacher_mask = input_ids.ne(pad_token_id)
        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = self.teacher(
                input_ids,
                attention_mask=teacher_mask,
                encoder_outputs=(teacher_enc_outputs, ),
                decoder_input_ids=decoder_input_ids,
                lm_labels=labels,
                output_hidden_states=not self.different_base_models,
                return_dict=True,
            )
        dec_mask = decoder_input_ids.ne(pad_token_id)
        loss_ce = self.calc_ce_loss(dec_mask, lm_logits, outputs.logits)
        if (not self.different_base_models) and self.alpha_hid > 0:  # Intermediate supervision of decoder hidden states
            tdec_hidden = outputs.decoder_hidden_states
            hid_loss_dec = self.calc_hidden_loss(
                dec_mask, dec_hidden, tdec_hidden, self.d_matches, normalize_hidden=self.hparams.normalize_hidden
            )
```

`self.different_base_models` is initialized in `__init__` in the same place as the earlier `self.do_calc_hidden_loss` as follows:

```
        self.different_base_models = True

        if hparams.student is None or hparams.teacher == hparams.student:
            self.different_base_models = False
            # Intermediate supervision: Decide which layers to supervise
            if hparams.supervise_forward:
                self.e_matches = get_layers_to_supervise(n_student=len(self.e_layer_ids), n_teacher=teacher_encoder_layers)
                self.d_matches = get_layers_to_supervise(n_student=len(self.d_layer_ids), n_teacher=teacher_decoder_layers)
            else:  # student layer should emulate hidden states of the teacher layer it was copied from
                self.e_matches = self.e_layer_ids
                self.d_matches = self.d_layer_ids

body:
This looks good, thanks for your contribution! I don't think the models need to be defined, however. They're basically a complete copy of the BART model, with no changes done to the configuration either. The main difference is the tokenizer.

Since https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/6995, tokenizers can be decoupled from their models, which would be ideal for this PR.

Instead of redefining all barthez models which are basically inheriting from BART, you would simply load the model checkpoint in the BART architecture. However, there would still be a `BarthezTokenizer` as this requires additional code.

You can take inspiration from the [Phobert](https://huggingface.co/vinai/phobert-base#) model. See how its [configuration](https://s3.amazonaws.com/models.huggingface.co/bert/vinai/phobert-base/config.json) file mentions that it is based on a RoBERTa implementation, but still leverages a `PhobertTokenizer` . You can see its implementation details [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/6129).

You can also take inspiration from Herbert [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/7798), which leveraged #6995 as well.

Update: after receiving a response from one of the authors (see issue above), I now understand how these are created in the original implementation (I actually implemented it in the wrong way with that dictionary). The correct way to do this (in case of a batch), is to set the `prev_label_ids` equal to `get_answer_ids(queries[index - 1])`, with index indicating whether the question is the first, second,... in a batch (note that a batch should always contain questions that refer to the same table). This function in turn calls `_get_answer_ids(column_ids, row_ids, question)`, with the column_ids and row_ids of the **current** table-question pair. So it's important that before calling `get_answer_ids`, the column_ids and row_ids are set to those of the current table-question pair.

This will require some changes, also to the signature of several methods (such as `get_answer_ids`, which is currently accepting a lot more parameters than just `question`), to reflect the [original implementation](https://github.com/google-research/tapas/blob/d8638f0909b3de32a85fe7491769d47d645d8e22/tapas/utils/tf_example_utils.py#L1155).

It is great that you deep dived into this issue and solved it, thank you! It seems like we're losing backwards compatibility on the `use_cache` parameter.

The new arguments are perfectly acceptable, but I think it would be nice to keep backwards compatibility. It should be easy enough by checking if there's a `use_cache` value in the configuration and setting it to the value of `use_mems`.

The following code does not output equal results on `master` and on this PR:

```py
from transformers import XLNetModel, XLNetTokenizer

model = XLNetModel.from_pretrained("xlnet-base-cased", use_cache=False)
tokenizer = XLNetTokenizer.from_pretrained("xlnet-base-cased")
inputs = tokenizer("Nice isn't it", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)
assert len(outputs) == 1
```
The assertion passes on `master`, but not on this branch.

This error will not ever be seen by the end user and that's precisely why it's there.

This check is not for the user, but for a developer who added must-have-this-available at run-time but forgot to add it to the dependency table. This exception shouldn't happen, but it's there to save grace for the developer. 

For example this will catch the situation where a dependency was added to `setup.py`, but then a developer forgot to run `python setup.py` to update the dependency table - since the key will be missing from the table. If we follow your suggestion to just tell install xyz this will not flag the developer that they haven't completed the process and the error will be wrong anyway, since chances are that the user already has it installed. since we aren't checking the version here, we are checking whether our code is synchronized.

It will also trap a mistyped name requirement - it will not do to suggest to the user to install `nupy` when the developer meant `numpy`. 



Let me know if it makes sense now.

The add-no-new-file-way is to hardcode the required versions in both setup.py and wherever we do the run-time checking. Based on my experience - the two will not stay in sync unless someone vigilantly ensures they do.

I also mentioned this is the only hurdle I see in this implementation - one still has to remember to run `python setup.py`  to keep things in sync. I don't really agree here -> I prefer to leave the `self.get_output_embeddings()` check here. E.g. `TFRag` won't be in any of the `TF_MODEL_FOR_CAUSAL_LM_MAPPING, TF_MODEL_FOR_MASKED_LM_MAPPING, TF_MODEL_FOR_SEQ_TO_SEQ_CAUSAL_LM_MAPPING`. And since `TFRag` will have two models of that can both generate, but won't both be able to be in the same MAPPING class we will already run into problems here. TFGPT2ForSequenceClassification uses the last token in order to do the classification. It would be great if you could take this PR as an opportunity to make sure this feature is enabled for `output_attentions` and `output_hidden_states` for all models in the lib. I would propose to add a test to `test_modeling_common.py` that looks as follows:

```python
    def test_retain_grad_hidden_states_attentions(self):
        config, inputs_dict = self.model_tester.prepare_config_and_inputs_for_common()
        config.output_hidden_states = True
        config.output_attentions = True

        # no need to test all models as different heads yield the same functionality
        model_class = self.all_model_classes[0]
        model = model_class(config)
        model.to(torch_device)

        inputs = self._prepare_for_class(inputs_dict, model_class)

        outputs = model(**inputs)
        first_output = outputs[0]

        if not config.is_encoder_decoder:
            first_hidden_states = outputs.hidden_states[0]
            first_attentions = outputs.attentions[0]

            first_hidden_states.retain_grad()
            first_attentions.retain_grad()

            first_output.flatten()[0].backward(retain_graph=True)

            self.assertIsNotNone(first_hidden_states.grad)
            self.assertIsNotNone(first_attentions.grad)

        else:
            first_encoder_hidden_states = outputs.encoder_hidden_states[0]
            first_encoder_attentions = outputs.encoder_attentions[0]
            first_encoder_hidden_states.retain_grad()
            first_encoder_attentions.retain_grad()

            first_decoder_hidden_states = outputs.decoder_hidden_states[0]
            first_decoder_attentions = outputs.decoder_attentions[0]
            first_decoder_hidden_states.retain_grad()
            first_decoder_attentions.retain_grad()

            first_output.flatten()[0].backward(retain_graph=True)

            self.assertIsNotNone(first_encoder_hidden_states.grad)
            self.assertIsNotNone(first_encoder_attentions.grad)
            self.assertIsNotNone(first_decoder_hidden_states.grad)
            self.assertIsNotNone(first_decoder_attentions.grad)
```

If Bart has this problem it is very likely that `FSTM` and `ProphetNet` have it as well actually...so this test would show this. 

Also we would have to do the same trick for the attentions in Bart, *e.g.* we could do the following change: 

```python
        if output_attentions:
            attn_weights_output = attn_weights.view(bsz, self.num_heads, tgt_len, src_len)
            attn_weights = attn_weights_output.view(bsz * self.num_heads, tgt_len, src_len)

        attn_probs = F.dropout(attn_weights, p=self.dropout, training=self.training)

        attn_output = self.out_proj(attn_output)

        return attn_output, attn_weights_output
```

in the `Attention` class of Bart.

I completely agree that in the normal use case, we shouldn't log things that go well.

However, to me, the `logging.info` behaves similary to a `--verbose` option you would have in a cli. 

In verbose mode, I think you would expect some logs both of what is going well and what is going wrong; it can help you build a timeline of events and explicitly tells you what did not fail. In my opinion it makes understanding logs easier.

As a fun example, using SSH with the -vvv option tells you:
```
[...]
debug2: ssh_connect_direct
debug1: Connecting to xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx [xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx] port 22.
debug1: Connection established.
[...]
```

following the approach that we should not log the things that go well, here the log `Connection established.` would be pointless. I don't think that's the case.

Pretty opinionated, so happy to be proven wrong!

body:
perhaps sticking to the commonly used abbreviations: dp/dpp? 

* dp = DataParallel
* ddp = DistributedDataParallel
* tpu = TPU 

and "single" is too ambiguous - single gpu or single process? 

Possible ideas:

* dnp = DataNotParallel (goes well with dp/dpp, but not mp/pp)
* np = NotParallel
* ds = DataSingle or DataSimple (possible confusion with DeepSpeed)
* sp = SimpleProcess (ambiguous processing unit-wise)
* ss = SinglegpuorcpuSingleprocess
* 11 = 1 cpu/gpu 1 process (variation of ss)
* pu = ProcessingUnit (G or C) (ambiguous process-wise)
* bu = Basic Unit
* one = one of cpu/gpu and of process (not an abbreviation, like the rest)
* basic = Well, basic (not an abbreviation, like the rest)
* simple = Same as basic (not an abbreviation, like the rest)

I think I like "**np**" the most - as it works well with **dp/ddp/mp/pp**

```suggestion
    @add_start_docstrings_to_model_forward(RAG_FORWARD_INPUTS_DOCSTRING)
    @replace_return_docstrings(output_type=TFRetrievAugLMOutput, config_class=_CONFIG_FOR_DOC)
    def call(
        self,
        input_ids,
        attention_mask=None,
        encoder_outputs=None,
        decoder_input_ids=None,
        decoder_attention_mask=None,
        past_key_values=None,
        doc_scores=None,
        context_input_ids=None,
        context_attention_mask=None,
        use_cache=None,
        output_attentions=None,
        output_hidden_states=None,
        output_retrieved=None,
        n_docs=None,
        training=False,
        **kwargs
    ):
        r"""
        Returns:

        Example::

            >>> from transformers import RagTokenizer, RagRetriever, RagModel
            >>> import torch

            >>> tokenizer = RagTokenizer.from_pretrained("facebook/rag-token-base")
            >>> retriever = RagRetriever.from_pretrained("facebook/rag-token-base", index_name="exact", use_dummy_dataset=True)
            >>> # initialize with RagRetriever to do everything in one forward call
            >>> model = TFRagModel.from_pretrained("facebook/rag-token-base", retriever=retriever, from_pt=True)

            >>> input_dict = tokenizer.prepare_seq2seq_batch("How many people live in Paris?", "In Paris, there are 10 million people.", return_tensors="tf")
            >>> input_ids = input_dict["input_ids"]
            >>> outputs = model(input_ids)

        """
        inputs = input_processing(
            func=self.call,
            config=self.config,
            input_ids=input_ids,
            attention_mask=attention_mask,
            encoder_outputs=encoder_outputs,
            decoder_input_ids=decoder_input_ids,
            decoder_attention_mask=decoder_attention_mask,
            past_key_values=past_key_values,
            doc_scores=doc_scores,
            context_input_ids=context_input_ids,
            context_attention_mask=context_attention_mask,
            use_cache=use_cache,
            output_attentions=output_attentions,
            output_hidden_states=output_hidden_states,
            output_retrieved=output_retrieved,
            n_docs=n_docs,
            training=training,
            kwargs_call=kwargs,
        )

        
        # whether retriever has to be used
        has_to_retrieve = (
            self.retriever is not None
            and (inputs["context_input_ids"] is None or inputs["context_attention_mask"] is None or inputs["doc_scores"] is None)
            and inputs["encoder_outputs"] is None
        )

        # encoder_outputs are pre-computed during RAG-token generation
        if inputs["encoder_outputs"] is None:

            if has_to_retrieve:
                question_enc_outputs = self.question_encoder(
                    inputs["input_ids"], attention_mask=inputs["attention_mask"], return_dict=True, training=inputs["training"]
                )
                # see https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/src/transformers/models/dpr/modeling_tf_dpr.py#L91
                question_encoder_last_hidden_state = question_enc_outputs[
                    0
                ]  # hidden states of question encoder => pooler_output

                retriever_outputs = self.retriever(
                    inputs["input_ids"],
                    question_encoder_last_hidden_state.numpy(),  # NEED_HELP : not work in GRAPH mode, tf.make_ndarray doesn't work as well
                    prefix=self.generator.config.prefix,
                    n_docs=inputs["n_docs"],
                    return_tensors="tf",
                )
                inputs["context_input_ids"], inputs["context_attention_mask"], retrieved_doc_embeds, retrieved_doc_ids = (
                    retriever_outputs["context_input_ids"],
                    retriever_outputs["context_attention_mask"],
                    retriever_outputs["retrieved_doc_embeds"],
                    retriever_outputs["doc_ids"],
                )

                # compute doc_scores
                inputs["doc_scores"] = tf.squeeze(
                    tf.matmul(
                        tf.expand_dims(question_encoder_last_hidden_state, axis=[1]),
                        retrieved_doc_embeds,
                        transpose_b=True,
                    ),
                    axis=[1],
                )

            else:
                assert (
                    inputs["context_input_ids"] is not None
                ), "Make sure that `context_input_ids` are passed, if no `retriever` is set. Alternatively, you can set a retriever using the `set_retriever(...)` function."
                assert (
                    inputs["context_attention_mask"] is not None
                ), "Make sure that `context_attention_mask` are passed, if no `retriever` is set. Alternatively, you can set a retriever using the `set_retriever(...)` function."
                assert (
                    inputs["doc_scores"] is not None
                ), "Make sure that `doc_scores` are passed, if no `retriever` is set. Alternatively, you can set a retriever using the `set_retriever(...)` function."

        assert (
            inputs["doc_scores"] is not None
        ), "Make sure that `doc_scores` are passed when passing `encoder_outputs` to the forward function."

        assert (
            inputs["doc_scores"].shape[1] % n_docs
        ) == 0, f" The first dimension of `context_input_ids` should be a multiple of `n_docs`={n_docs}, but is {context_input_ids.shape[0]}."

        # Decoder input without context documents
        if inputs["decoder_input_ids"] is not None:
            inputs["decoder_input_ids"] = tf.repeat(inputs["decoder_input_ids"], inputs["n_docs"], axis=0)

        if inputs["decoder_attention_mask"] is not None:
            inputs["decoder_attention_mask"] = tf.repeat(inputs["decoder_attention_mask"], inputs["n_docs"], axis=0)

        gen_outputs = self.generator(
            inputs["context_input_ids"],
            attention_mask=inputs["context_attention_mask"],
            encoder_outputs=inputs["encoder_outputs"],
            decoder_input_ids=inputs["decoder_input_ids"],
            decoder_attention_mask=inputs["decoder_attention_mask"],
            past_key_values=inputs["past_key_values"],
            use_cache=inputs["use_cache"],
            return_dict=True,
            training=inputs["training"],
        )

        if not has_to_retrieve:
            question_encoder_last_hidden_state = None
            question_enc_hidden_states = None
            question_enc_attentions = None
            retrieved_doc_embeds = None
            retrieved_doc_ids = None
        else:
            question_enc_hidden_states = question_enc_outputs.hidden_states
            question_enc_attentions = question_enc_outputs.attentions

        if not has_to_retrieve or not output_retrieved:
            # don't output retrieved docs
            inputs["context_input_ids"] = (None,)
            inputs["context_attention_mask"] = None
            retrieved_doc_embeds = None
            retrieved_doc_ids = None

        return TFRetrievAugLMOutput(
            logits=gen_outputs.logits,
            doc_scores=inputs["doc_scores"],
            past_key_values=gen_outputs.past_key_values,
            context_input_ids=inputs["context_input_ids"],
            context_attention_mask=inputs["context_attention_mask"],
            retrieved_doc_embeds=retrieved_doc_embeds,
            retrieved_doc_ids=retrieved_doc_ids,
            question_encoder_last_hidden_state=question_encoder_last_hidden_state,
            question_enc_hidden_states=question_enc_hidden_states,
            question_enc_attentions=question_enc_attentions,
            generator_enc_last_hidden_state=gen_outputs.encoder_last_hidden_state,
            generator_enc_hidden_states=gen_outputs.encoder_hidden_states,
            generator_enc_attentions=gen_outputs.encoder_attentions,
            generator_dec_hidden_states=gen_outputs.decoder_hidden_states,
            generator_dec_attentions=gen_outputs.decoder_attentions,
        )
```

body:
yes, I forgot to delete `key_padding_mask`. It's not needed anymore. The `atn_mask` for `BartAttention` is the final attention mask that is a merge of  the causal mask and the key padding mask. Since we always merge the attention masks to a 4d Tensor and pass this one to the attention layer, I've done the same in Bart. 

There are a bunch of tests that would fail if the causal mask is wrong, *e.g.* https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/9d7d0005b046a95d9d59354714bb6c3547a612fe/tests/test_modeling_bart.py#L459 and I've also added an aggressive test verifying that causal mask and attn mask works as expected (`test_decoder_model_past_with_large_inputs`)

body: No need of an error or warning, as now, we allow tensors that have a different name. We don't have the choice because all the tensors that will be represented by a symbolic input simply cannot have a name that belongs to the parameters. So basically a warning will be raised everytime you will use a tf.data.dataset and for each batch of the dataset, it will simply pollute your standard output for nothing.

More specifically in the example given here https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/8985#issuecomment-740654016

the symbolic inputs are:
```
input_ids = tf.keras.Input(shape=(128,), dtype='int32', name="input_ids")
attention_mask = tf.keras.Input(shape=(128, ), dtype='int32', name="attention_mask")
```

And the tensors that represents there symbolic inputs are respectively named `IteratorGetNext:0` and `IteratorGetNext:1` and these two names cannot be changed.

body:
This model, at least how the code looks like, is not graph compliant (for example there are several `.numpy()` that cannot be run in a graph, including some conditions that are not properly setup, the usage of `.shape` that is unstable in graph mode, some keywords arguments that are not properly handled, etc...). So basically you cannot properly train it, without specifying that you want it to be run in eager mode. Hence, not possible to get a clean saved model, no proper training, almost no grappler optimizations, etc... compared to all the others. That's why I'm not very picky on the review ^^

To be sure, you can disable the eager execution with `tf.compat.v1.disable_eager_execution()` and try to run a simple inference. If an error is raised it means that your model is not graph compliant. (This is my case)

So I would like this to be specified in the documentation, this is mostly to make the users aware of this context.

Nevertheless, that's nice to be able to run it without the need of a retriever, this makes things much easier to have this model in "proper" TensorFlow. Then, if you want to have it fully graph compliant I'm 100% for it but the model needs more rework. Do you want me to help with this? 😃

Hi @stefan-it, thanks a lot for your contribution!

If Bort can be loaded seamlessly in the BERT architecture, is there really a need to redefine all models in PyTorch and TensorFlow? We would need to do this for all models on the hub if that was the case. body:
There is a subtlety for generation that is a bit complex, but that should be documented here IMO. 

_Short context:_
For generation, usually only "decoder-only" models are used *a.k.a* GPT2, or the decoder of T5, Bart, etc...
"decoder-only" models use uni-directional self-attention meaning that previously projected past key and value states can be re-used and don't have to be calculated again => thus we can save computation this way. We have this feature enabled with the `use_cache` flag. So to compare what happens in the model, let's first see how generation works for `use_cache=False` (assuming that one word == one token):

step 1: [This is the prompt] -> decoder transfo -> [logit_1 logit_2 logit_3 logit_4] (each word was mapped to corresponding logit: logit_2 is output logit of "is" => in generation we sample next word from last logit (that's how LM works) => use logit_4 to sample <gen_word_1>
step 2: [This is the prompt <gen_word_1>] -> decoder transfo -> [logit_1(of this) logit_2 logit_3 logit_4 logit_5] => use logit_5 to sample <gen_word_2> 
step 3: [This is the prompt <gen_word_1> <get_word_2>] ...

Now however if `use_cache` is enabled the following happens:

step 1: [This is the prompt] -> decoder transfo -> [logit_1 logit_2 logit_3 logit_4] (each word was mapped to corresponding logit: logit_2 is output logit of "is" => in generation we sample next word from last logit (that's how LM works) => use logit_4 to sample <gen_word_1> **and** past key values of "This is the prompt" is returned as well. Here `past_key_values` has a length of 4
step 2: pass past_key_values **and**  [<gen_word_1>] -> decoder transfo -> [logit_5] => use logit_5 to sample <gen_word_2> **and** past key values are extended to have a length of 5
step 3: pass past_key_values of len 5 **and** [<gen_word_2>] ...
....

=> so now the relevant conclusion:

`hidden_states` has a length of `(batch_size, sequence_length, hidden_size)` if *no* `past_key_values` are passed, but has a length of `(batch_size, 1, hidden_size)` if past_key_values are passed. Similarly `attentions` is of size `(batch_size, num_heads, sequence_length, sequence_length)` and with `past_key_values` that are passed it's of size `(batch_size, num_heads, sequence_length, 1)`

Hope this helps a bit to understand the deal with `past_key_values`.

I'd suggest to slightly changed the description to 

```" ... of shape :obj:`(batch_size, num_heads, sequence_length, sequence_length)` if no ``past_key_values`` are passed and of shape :obj:`(batch_size, num_heads, sequence_length, 1)` if ``past_key_values`` are passed. ``past_key_values`` are returned when ``use_cache=True``.

"```
 
We should do this change for all `attentions`, `hidden_states` and `decoder_attentions`, `decoder_hidden_states`, **but** not for `encoder_hidden_states`

Ok, now we have to add the ugly hack to keep backwards compatibility! Would be nice to get @sgugger and @LysandreJik input here as well. 

Context:
Similar to the model's forward method we should add `GenerationOutputs` to generate. It's way more problematic to handle the backwards compatibility here though IMO. As one can see in the above line, we previously just returned a single tensor `input_ids`. Now with the `GenerationOutputs` we have to change this to a "tuple-like" output. The question now is how to implement this feature without **any** breaking backward compatibility since `generate()` is such a public method. It's not sufficient to just check return `input_ids` when all `output_attentions`, `output_hidden_states`, `output_scores` are false and return the `GenerationOutputs` otherwise because people might previously had `config.output_attentions` set to `True`. In the long run, I want to force `generate()` to always return a `GenerationOutput`, but for now I think we have to add some flag like `return_generation_dict` only to the `generate` function that defaults to `False` and that has to be set to `True` to return the new `GenerationOutput` class. Then we should update all our examples to have the flag set to `True` and show the new API. In a next step we could add a depreciation warning that somewhat forcing the user to set `return_generation_dict` to `True` and eventually we delete this flag. Not sure if that's the best approach....keen to hear your thoughts @sgugger, @LysandreJik, @SBrandeis

body:
for `roberta` Position numbers begin at `padding_idx+1` as stated in the doc string here 
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/f4432b7e01dc46008fb823096d884bdc2861b49c/src/transformers/models/roberta/modeling_roberta.py#L1360-L1364



so the input shouldn't start with pad token. If `past_key_values` are used and if the input starts with pad token then the position ids are off by one. i.e

If it starts with pad and `past_key_values` is not used, position_ids become  `[1, 2, 3, 4...]`

but if `past_key_values` are used then for the second position the position id will be 3 since we add past_key_values_length to it and there is no way to know if the first token was pas token.

body:
If we follow my approach:
- For `CausalLMOutputWithCrossAttentions` this would mean -> no breaking changes for `GPT2` as all indexing and output length stay the same, only the class name is changed from `CausalLMOutputWithPastAndCrossAttentions` to `CausalLMOutputWithCrossAttentions`. For all other models *a.k.a* `RobertaForCausalLM`, `BertForCausalLM` and `BertGenerationDecoder` -> the output class is changed and the default behavior is to now have an additional `past_key_values` output by default (`use_cache=True` by default in those classes). So the difference from now to my approach is that in my approach the **type** of the output class stays the same while currently the type is changed. Also note that these models are only really used in EncoderDecoder settings (there are no pre-trained weights for decoder-only Bert models) so that those models are expected to have `past_key_values` as an output.
- For `BaseModelOutputWithPoolingAndCrossAttentions`, the default case stays the same. Only if `self.is_decoder=True` which is not the default case, will the `past_key_values` by part of the output. 

=> IMO, we can/should reuse the names `CausalLMOutputWithCrossAttentions` and `BaseModelOutputWithPoolingAndCrossAttentions`, **not** introduce `BaseModelOutputWithPoolingAndPastAndCrossAttentions` and delete `CausalLMOutputWithPastAndCrossAttentions`. It is more concise in terms of naming, IMO, it doesn't introduce more breaking changes as new names would have and it also forces us to directly implement the caching in the future.

body:
The comment for APEX is because the `to` method is lso used to convert the `dtype` of a Tensor, and APEX does not perform type checks before calling the to method (just that the to method exists), which means or `BatchEncoding` are converted to a dict of half tensors if we don't have this safeguard.

Using an `int` should work with older versions of PyTorch AFAICT, however it's considered "legacy" behavior so it may be removed in a future version. In the meantime, I have no problem with accepting them on our side.

body: cc @patil-suraj @ibeltagy  -> we should probalby apply this to all seq2seq models. The cached cross-attention states never need to be re-ordered since they're always identical for all `beam_idx`. Since re-ordering relies on `index_select` which creates a new tensor in PT this re-ordering can actually consume a lot of memory. In the case of `Led` this saved ~2GB of RAM because the encoder_hidden_states can be **very** large

body:
e.g.:

The assertion line is the error message that the program prints when it fails. This is an example of an assertion line and it typically includes a traceback:

  ```python
   Traceback (most recent call last):
     File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
     File "/transformers/src/transformers/__init__.py", line 34, in <module>
       from . import dependency_versions_check
     File "/transformers/src/transformers/dependency_versions_check.py", line 34, in <module>
       from .file_utils import is_tokenizers_available
     File "/transformers/src/transformers/file_utils.py", line 40, in <module>
       from tqdm.auto import tqdm
   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tqdm.auto'
   ```

If you received this error search:
   1. first for `"huggingface" "transformers" "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tqdm.auto'"`
   2. if you don't find relevant results, then search for just `"ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tqdm.auto'"`
   3. and finally if nothing still comes up, then remove the outside quotes: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tqdm.auto'`

If the error includes any error messages that include bits of your filesystem, always remove those in the search query since other users will not have the same bits as yours. For example:
  ```bash
python -c 'open("/tmp/wrong_path.txt", "r")'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/tmp/wrong_path.txt'
```
Here you'd search for just: `"FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory"`

If your local information bits that you removed were inside the error message and you removed them you may need to remove double quotes since your query is no longer exact.

body:
So this change deals with the case where devices aren't necessarily ordered by ID. That is the case where a device_map's keys are say, `[0,2,1,3]` for whatever reason.

The only issue here is that only starting from py37 we get ordered dicts and all is good, so for py36, unless it is a cython-built we have an issue that 0th item might not be the 0th item in the device map. Not sure how to deal with it.

Or alternatively we need to assert if the order is not numericaly rising, but again we have an issue with the dict, before py37.

Perhaps the simplest thing is to say that MP requires py > 3.6

Or the user needs to build the `device_map` using `collections.OrderedDict`.

We could check in the  `device_map` validation function whether the passed `device_map` is either `collections.OrderedDict` or py > 3.6 or assert otherwise.

The order of the signature arguments IMO should be as follows:

```python
                expected_arg_names = [
                    "input_ids",
                    "attention_mask",
                    "decoder_input_ids",
                    "decoder_attention_mask",
                    "head_mask",
                    "decoder_head_mask",
                    "encoder_outputs",
                ]
```

The reason is that `decoder_input_ids` is more important than `head_mask` for torchscript.

We models like Bart we would still like to be able to use torchscript as follows:

```python
traced_bart(input_ids, attention_mask, decoder_input_ids, decoder_attention_mask)
```

instead of having to do

```python
traced_bart(input_ids, attention_mask, head_mask, decoder_input_ids, decoder_attention_mask)
```

where as `head_mask` would have to be a tensor of all 1's since in 99% of the times it's not used for torchscript.

So it'd be great if we can slightly change the order in all `...Model` and all `...ForConditionalGeneration` models so that we have:

```python
                expected_arg_names = [
                    "input_ids",
                    "attention_mask",
                    "decoder_input_ids",
                    "decoder_attention_mask",
                    "head_mask",
                    "decoder_head_mask",
                    "encoder_outputs",
                ]
```

`head_mask` is just used to little for torchscript so that we have to break the (first all encoder inputs, then all decoder inputs) logic here. 

We can adapt the test as follows:

```python
...
            arg_names = [*signature.parameters.keys()]
            if model.config.is_encoder_decoder:
                expected_arg_names = [
                    "input_ids",
                    "attention_mask",
                    "decoder_input_ids",
                    "decoder_attention_mask",
                ]

                expected_arg_names.extend(["head_mask", "decoder_head_mask", "encoder_outputs"] if "head_mask" in arg_names else ["encoder_outputs"])
                ...
```

It probably depends on how it's implemented. 

If it's a single paragraph we are looking at then it can be parsed directly into an optional header and a bullet list, then you immediately know whether there are multiple bullets or just one. so a hypothetical parser could go:

header, items = parse_to_bullet_list(para)

```
Bounding Boxes of each input sequence tokens. Selected in the range ``[0, config.max_2d_position_embeddings
            - 1]``. blah blahof each input sequence tokens. Selected in the range ``[0, something_else
            - 5]``.

The goal was to have an internet free tokenizer. (I was coding in the train so I really could not use internet there).

I could most definitely make a tokenizer from an existing class but that would require defining a vocabulary on the fly.

The biggest problem with a real tokenizer is the fact that the model is randomly initialized so guaranteeing the output is harder to do. Setting a seed might work, but I don't like to rely on that for tests as it tends to no work as good. Here I simply discard the actual output of the model and simply rely on the shapes.

I do agree that using a Dummy here might be overkill because we need to re implement a lot of functionality and we're not going to be sure that there's not a change between the two implementations.

Would:
- Using an in code vocabulary
- Setting a manual seed
be better in your opinion ?

However, if you really want to go down the road of internet-free tokenizers, we do build some of them in the tokenization tests. Either by using the SentencePiece models in `tests/fixtures/` (see [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/tests/test_tokenization_albert.py#L41) an example for ALBERT's tokenizer), or by using an in-code vocabulary as you mention (see [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/tests/test_tokenization_bert.py#L44-L78) an example for BERT's tokenizer).

Regarding the randomly initialized model, you can also use a `tiny` variant of a model, which we create specifically for tests. There are already a bunch on the hub, and they sound less dangerous than setting a seed in a test that could potentially have side-effects on other tests down the road.

body:
I'm very happy with the "one-line" fix that solves the problem stated in the issue - this looks clean!

However, there are some other things here where I'm not sure if they are part of the fix or why they are done:
1) The attention logic is changed in TFLongformer. Why is that done? This has nothing to do with s2s, so should not be in this PR, no? Also, if we have to change it -> I think we should change it in a cleaner way. 
2) In general I really don't like the `tf.cond(condition, do_fn_one, do_fn_two)` design. I think I understand that it is sometimes necessary, but I really like to keep the usage of this function to a minimum in general. The functional approach is very different to our general library design and make the code much much harder to read. It always creates an abstraction by having to wrap parts of the code into a function with no args, like `def attn_mask_from_inp_ids()` which is not easy to follow and to me always looks like a hack. In Bart we manage to do this part of the code without the usage of `tf.cond` and Bart has the same exact logic as LED has there -> so we can make it easier I think. 
3) I prefer having a logging function to be displayed for both cases over creating a "fake" logging function that doesn't do anything. I think it's fine to log "No padding required" in LED over creating a "hacky" "fake" logging function. The more we add those things to the library, the more the community will use such "hacky" functions as well which is not the right way IMO

This is OK, we can indeed remove the `drop_rows_to_fit` parameter of `TapasTokenizer`, however we also have a parameter called `cell_trim_length`, which will only have an effect in case the tokenizer is used with `truncation=True`. So we should update its documentation. Currently it says:

"`cell_trim_length` (int, optional, defaults to -1) - If > 0: Trim cells so that the length is <= this value. Also disables further cell trimming, should thus be used with `drop_rows_to_fit` below."

=> we can update this to:
"`cell_trim_length` (int, optional, defaults to -1) - If > 0: Trim cells so that the length is <= this value. Also disables further cell trimming, should thus be used with `truncation` set to to `True`."

body:
While printing can get things done, I think there are better ways to go about it, which may be a bit more complex to setup, but end up being **so** useful as development goes on.

When porting a model, I like to:
- Isolate the different forward passes that are useful, in a step-by-step manner. This means that I like to proceed as follows:
    - Have a way to retrieve the embeddings
    - Have a way to retrieve each layer's output
    - Have a way to retrieve the Transformer output
    - Have a way to retrieve the full model output, for each head
- All of these output should be gathered into a single script, in **variables**. This can be a pain to setup, but makes it so much simpler in the end because you can **compare** values.
- These values should be compared to the implementation in HuggingFace Transformers. A relative/absolute difference can be defined

Having this step-by-step approach with the ability to compare is imo incredibly useful because:
- You can check the results algorithmically, rather than checking the terminal output and verifying the results
- You can set this up very early on, starting with the embeddings
- You can ensure you have no regression when working on the model, as when finishing up the last head, you'll still be checking the embeddings. You'll be checking all heads at once, too.

Here's an example of how I did it with ELECTRA: [compare_electra.py](https://gist.github.com/LysandreJik/db4c948f6b4483960de5cbac598ad4ed). It's slightly more complicated to setup but I think it's worthwhile.

I have no idea how you would explain this in the document, so feel free to ignore if it's not appropriate :)

body:
Boy, this was a monumental work, @patrickvonplaten! Absolutely phenomenal work!

I left a bunch of small suggestions - please feel free to ignore any or all, no need for any justifications.

Wrt delivery, I felt it may be a bit overwhelming with the amount of information. So I highly recommend to add numbers to the sub-sections so that it's easier for one to know where they are at. It's super-detailed, which is great, but also one could get scared with so many details. Perhaps even adding a clear Table of Contents with numbered items, so the reader knows, ok, I'm at 6/10, like in a book. 

In my experience I used a very different approach to porting, because I have a hard time working in vacuum which this approach suggests. To me I need to see a constant success, while progressing towards a bigger goal. So my approach was to have 2 code bases side-by-side, with 2 small scripts, using real text and not just a few numbers and porting the tokenizer first, so I at each step I was matching the ported code with the original, rather than work on each separately. 
That's why it was important for me to choose checkpoints that used languages I speak.

But there is more than one way to skin-the-cat, and my approach is documented in my blog post, albeit it's outdated now since many things have changed in the code layout since it was written.

Sorry, yeah this was my bad. I didn't get why we've inputted both `decoder_input_ids` and `labels` previously - should have thought about it a bit more!

It's a tough decision on how to solve this long-term I think:

- there is no guarantee that `shift_tokens_right` is the same for all models, we already have three different methods (MBart, EncoderDecoder (not yet implemented but will be different), Bart & other enc-dec)
- We don't really want to start an `if isinstance(self.tokenizer)`-else cascade in the data collactor.
- I don't really like to add a flag `_do_compute_loss` to the encoder-decoder models because it breaks consistency that only passing `lables` will trigger a loss calculation with all other models and adds more complexity to the user in that another config param has to be understood.
- Another option would be to pass the models to the `__init__` of the data collator and then to call: `decoder_input_ids = model.shift_right(...)` and forcing all functions to have the same name similar to `prepare_inputs_for_generation(...)` 
- I think overall, it would actually be better to get fully rid of the data collators all together and instead make use of `datasets.map(...)` to prepare the inputs and just use the default datacollator as shown in https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/ca422e3d7d8086baf233993af2f6f90f30729933/src/transformers/data/data_collator.py#L35 => then we wouldn't have any of those problems and would have more control over what to input to the model

Maybe we should discuss this quickly offline
author: patrickvonplaten

body:
Looks good to me for now! However, the script won't work with ProphetNet and LED at the moment I think. 

As discussed a bit offline: 

I don't think specific data collators are a good solution. One can fully prepare the data using datasets.map() function (I always do this in my seq2seq scripts) and then just use the default data collator that simply stacks the tensors correctly to a batch. We will run into more and more problems using specific data collators like the Seq2Seq ones because they can never handle all cases, e.g. it wouldn't work at the moment for LED either because LED needs to define a global_attention_mask as an input. Also thinking a bit more about the expansion to Vision and Speech for Transformers where we will have even more different kinds of inputs, I don't think that we should rely on a data collator to map the raw data to the model's expected input. It'll end up in a weird if-else cascade anyways. I think the responsibility should shift to the datasets.map(...) function to define all required inputs. So, regarding the PR, to keep bcp I'm fine with adding some kind of hack to `Seq2SeqDatacollator` to make it work, but I'm not really in favor of adding a boolean flag to the model. I'd rather like to deprecate the Seq2SeqDatacollator soon and just make all scripts use the default_data_collator - I think all scripts already do, but some use more data collators in addition.

Would be keen to hear @LysandreJik @stas00 @patil-suraj @thomwolf opinion here as well

body:
I have just stumbled upon the same bug. Torch ONNX tracer [converts](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/onnx.html#torch.onnx.operators.shape_as_tensor) `torch.Shape` values from scalars to `torch.Tensor`, which is somehow manipulated by the tracer as the graph is being executed. In this particular case the value of `seq_length` variable, which is now a tensor, changes between the moment it was declared and the moment it was used in the code above.

I'm suspect the change above is using `num_heads` instead of `seq_length`. While it may work, it may not be correct. I suggest to do this instead:

```python
position_bias_seq_length = scores.shape[2]
position_bias = position_bias[:, :, -position_bias_seq_length:, :]
```

because the next line adds the bias to the scores:

```python
scores += position_bias
```

Let me know if I should submit a separate PR.

body:
Thanks a lot for making MBart50 work! I think we should use this PR as an opportunity to clean up the `adjust_logits_during_generation` function. This function is pretty ugly and only exists for Bart-like Fairseq models. It should not exist and instead be a `LogitsProcessor` object called `ForceTokenProcessor`. We can do this refactoring as follows -> we create a new `generate()` argument, called `forced_pos_id_pairs: Optional[Dict]` that will contain all pos: token pairs, such as `{2: 0, 141: 2}` meaning that at position 2 the bos_token_id should be generated and at position 141 the eos_token_id should be generated. Then this dict will the input of:

```python
class LogitsProcessor(self):

def __init__(self, pos_id_pairs):
     self.pos_id_pairs = pos_id_pairs

__call__(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, scores: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    next_token_id = input_ids.shape[-1] + 1
    if next_token_id in self.pos_id_pairs:
          mask = torch.full_like(scores, -math.inf)
          mask[:, self.pos_id_pairs[next_token_id]] = 0
          scores += mask
    return scores
```

This functionality should then cover all the necessary edge cases and we can delete `adjust_logits_during_generation` completely (we need to set `forced_pos_id_pairs` correctly to avoid breaking changes).

Another benefit of this approach would be that we don't have to pass `prefix` down to all generate methods.

body:
Thanks for the PR!

First and foremost, please use two different PRs when adding two different pieces of functionality. The generate part/refactor is independent from MBart50 as far as I can tell so it should be in its own PR. This make reviews easier and if one of the two things ends up breaking one slow test or makes a regression down the line, it's going to be hard to figure out which part did.

On the general seq2seq models API, a decision was taken to deprecate and remove the `prepare_seq2seq_batch` method, so we should not use it in new docstrings and examples. We should also hunt existing docstrings and examples to remove any mention of it sooner rather than later. The method itself will be deprecated once `finetune_trainer` goes to legacy.

On the mBART/mBART50 API, the language ids should be attributes of the tokenizer that are set at init, and that the user can change at any time. The context manager `as_target_tokenizer` will adapt the special tokens while taking into account the target language automatically, for the src language, the attribute should have a setter to call `set_src_lang_special_tokens` when the attribute is changed.
With this, everything should work properly without needing `prepare_seq2seq_batch` (as long as the user changes the attributes when they want to change language, which is pretty intuitive IMO).
author: sgugger

`tokenizer.prepasre_seq2seq_batch` should never be advertised anymore. For `mBART` and `mBART-50`, the `src_lang` and `tgt_lang` should just be attributes the user can:
- set at init
- change whenever their languages change (not sure it happens a lot in a script)

Then the traditional call should be used for encoding the inputs, and the traditional call should be used within the contextmanager `as_target_tokenizer` for encoding the targets.
